propositions: Committed locks freeze transitive dependencies, causing any subsequently-published advisory against a pinned version to block unrelated changes in CI until the advisory is resolved

uv's universal resolution locks every extra jointly, so a single capping dependency in an extra holds the whole project on a vulnerable version even when the vulnerable package is not directly required

constraint-dependencies can only narrow an existing constraint set and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output; it does not prove an upgrade is impossible and override-dependencies is the correct instrument to replace an offending requirement

Gerrit verify should block on an advisory only when a change touches the dependency map (uv.lock or pyproject.toml), not when it is an unrelated change, while scheduled main-lane runs must fail visibly on outstanding advisories and block releases

A periodic scheduled canary must notice when an override-dependencies justification condition has been met and automatically file and close tracking tickets to prevent stale suppressions from accumulating silently

The runbook must document pip-audit retry behavior (only DB-UNREACHABLE failures are recheckable; recheck cannot clear a real finding), severity thresholds (CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warns, LOW tracked), and evidence required before overriding an upstream cap
